STEP 1 - Scene: Two halves of boiled or steamed corn on the cob (sweet corn), on a white oval/triangular serving dish. Photographed from above at a slight angle, close-up.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a white serving dish roughly 30 cm long at its longest undistorted width. Taking it as a platter about 28 cm long and 18 cm wide, the corn cobs are each about 6-7 cm wide and about 5 cm long across the cut face. The cob sections are roughly 5 cm in diameter (cut face width) and about 5-6 cm long each.

STEP 3 - Items: Two cut corn-on-the-cob pieces (kernel sections). No sauce or butter visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Dish area roughly 400 cm^2. Each corn piece covers about 6% (about 25 cm^2 footprint); together about 12% of the dish.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each piece is roughly a cylinder ~5 cm diameter x ~5.5 cm long, so about 108 cm^3 each, but the pieces are rounded and partly hollow in appearance; estimate ~90 ml each, ~180 ml total.

STEP 6 - Grams: Corn kernels/cob sections are a cut-vegetable-like dense item; use bulk density ~0.7 g/ml (cob pieces include cob core and air gaps). 180 ml x 0.7 ≈ 125 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Sweet corn, boiled, is about 96 kcal per 100 g. 125 g x 0.96 ≈ 120 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two short cob halves on a platter, roughly 100-130 g, around 100-120 kcal, is plausible. Total: about 125 g, about 120 kcal.
